lines.trans: You're one busy man—here to apologize this time?
I will get the money without fail. Please, I beg you not to cancel our contract.
Why don't you just give up on satellite and liquidate the whole thing?

words.gram: Past た-form of する (to do/happen).

lines.trans: It is my company's lifeline—and it is my dream.
What is the largest sum of money you have ever lost in the shortest time?
The other day I lost thirty billion yen in a mere two minutes when our satellite rocket launch failed.
Twenty years of development—rocket history is a battle with failure, and we lost big again.

words.gram: Past tense of plain copula だ.

lines.trans: Then you can just take on the challenge again, right?
I'm getting off here. I intend to resign from the company too.
Hey wait—how can you quit like that?!
I've come to hate that word challenge. If we hadn't tried, we'd still have the money.

words.gram: Past た-form of なる (to become).

lines.trans: If you ever change your mind, get off too. I'll be waiting for you, Muranishi.

words.gram: Noun in the idiom 気が向く (feel like doing).
